findings.failure_path: Give one owner a net-deleting row labeled source-refuted with the required URL and pointer, plus an unrelated behavior change labeled semantic-control with observed-failure:no and a valid firing locator. Both rows are row_valid, and evaluated.any? finds the source-refuted row, so the cumulative owner passes without any RED row even though it is neither wording-only nor an identifier rename—the exact hiding path this floor previously blocked.
findings.smallest_fix: Make the source-refuted floor exemption owner-wide, for example requiring every non-no-behavior row in the cumulative owner scope to be source-refuted; add same-round and cross-round source-refuted plus semantic-control regression cases.

concern_results.conclusion: Failed: one valid source-refuted row now exempts the entire owner from the RED floor, including unrelated semantic-control changes.
No direct data or permission mutation is added, but the shared-gate trust boundary is weakened enough to permit false-green acceptance.
A net-deleting source-refuted row combined with a valid semantic-control row passes every row check and the owner-wide floor without any RED evidence.

The synthetic cases omit mixed source-refuted plus semantic-control rows and cumulative multi-round owners, so they do not detect the bypass. Case F also exercises only RED-baseline, not every existing class named by its acceptance criterion.
Existing status syntax remains compatible; the material regression is the loss of the prior owner-level evidence invariant.
There is no irreversible migration, but this shared-gate change is not release-ready until the owner-wide exemption is constrained and regression-tested.
The bypass produces a successful gate result, so existing failure diagnostics provide no visibility or recovery signal.
Containment fails because a per-row, round-scoped source-refuted result is promoted through any? into proof for the whole cumulative owner diff.
